aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Regulations Related To Country Or Region

aas:langStringTextType.aas:text: Regulatory information related to country or region: What country the information applies to, stated as a code in accordance to ISO 3166 (two letters). This defines which SDSs can be derived from this file. (A SDS may be written in English, and the information given may be in accordance to Norwegian regulations).

In fact, this is a product data set, i.e. data for a collection of safety data sheets for the same product.
In fact, this is a product data set, i.e. data for a collection of safety data sheets for the same product.
Identification data for the substance/mixture, uses and supplier.

At least one instance (with empty UserId) for the identification as delivered by the supplier. Use more instances for various package sizes, various products in a group SDS, or (with filled UserId) for reference to relabelled products of the SDS recipient. Also for group safety data sheets, each instance of TradeProductIdentity covers one substance or product. When importing, make sure that SDScom documents are not automatically replaced if the product identity is the same! GTINs are not necessarily unique (they should, but aren't in practice!), and product identities may refer to kits with multiple products and SDSs. Unique IDs that allow automatic overriding of data require a bilateral agreement between customer and supplier and should be placed in ProductNo.

Physical and chemical properties: This section of the safety data sheet shall describe the empirical data relating to the substance or mixture, if relevant. In the case of a mixture, the entries shall clearly indicate to which substance in the mixture the data apply, unless it is valid for the whole mixture. The following properties shall be clearly identified including, where appropriate, a reference to the test methods used and specification of appropriate units of measurement and/or reference conditions. If relevant for the interpretation of the numerical value, the method of determination shall also be provided.

Stability and reactivity: The section shall describe the stability of the chemical and the possibility of hazardous reactions occurring under certain conditions of use, also if released into the environment. Where appropriate, include a reference to the test methods used. If a particular property does not apply or if information is not available, the reasons shall be given.

Reactivity description: The reactivity hazards of the chemical shall be described. Specific test data shall be provided where available. Information may also be based on general data for the class or family of substance or mixture if such data adequately represent the anticipated hazard.If data for mixtures are not available, data on substances in the mixture shall be provided.

Disposal considerations: The section shall describe information for proper waste management of the chemical and/or its container to assist in the determination of safe and environmentally preferred waste management options, consistent with the requirements in accordance with EU and national legislation. Information relevant for the safety of persons conducting waste management activities shall complement the information given in Section 8. The information on the waste management measures shall be consistent with the identified uses. If the disposal of the chemical presents a danger, a description of the residues and their safe handling shall be given.

Waste treatment: Specify the appropriate methods of disposal of both the chemical and any contaminated packaging. The actual use of the chemical will often influence the classification of the waste. Waste treatment containers and methods shall be specified including the appropriate methods of waste treatment of both the chemical and any contaminated packaging (e.g. incineration, recycling, landfilling). Physical or chemical properties that may affect waste treatment options shall be specified. Sewage disposal shall be discouraged. Where appropriate, any special precautions for any recommended waste treatment option shall be identified.

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: The SDScom root element

The version of the eSDScom standard which is applied in the transmission of information. This version number also denotes the minimum version number for eSDScom phrase IDs referenced in the XML file. For backward compatibility, the tag name is still SDScom, although the standard now includes ESCom exposure scenarios and is thus named eSDScom.
Reference to the SDScomXML subsets SDScomBau and SDScomChem containing SDSComXML fields. More informaion to SDScomBau and SDScomChem are available at www.sdbtransfer.de
Phrase catalogue Name, eg. EuPhraC
Phrase catalogue issuer: Identification of the suppler of the phrase catalogue to the exporting system, eg. EuPhraC-Workinggroup.

Catalogue version: The version no of the phrase catalog the information is based on to identify the actual version of the phrase catalogue applied. Phrase catalogues are updated more or less regularly, and different versions may show some differences.
Date of release of the catalogue version: The version timestamp of the phrase catalogue the information is based on
Identifier of the phrase catalogue used.

Phrase catalogue: The phrase library(ies) applied in the preparation of the information. The optional attribute PhraseCatalogueId allows multiple catalogues to be used. Phrase must then have an attribute specifying the PhraseCatalogueId.

If languages are used in more than one country, there might be national flavours that are significantly different (like pt-BR, en-US). In this case, indicate the country here. If empty, this field defaults to the originating country (pt-PT, en-GB).

GTIN No, in Europe also known as EAN. Has max. 1 instance in an ideal world.

This is the place to describe kits. If the data describes a product P which is part of kit K, create two instances of ProductIdentity: One for P, and one for K with an entry in ProductDefinition that describes "This Product is a kit. The data describes one part of the kit."
Packaging type, e.g. bottle, canister, drum, IBC or box.

aas:valueReferencePair.aas:value: tea bag (product disperses through the container when added to water)

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Further specifies the material and type of packaging.
Comparison sign or symbol for the exact value, e.g. =, ca., < or >.
Exact numeric value of the package size or quantity; unit in the associated field.
Comparison sign for the upper value, e.g. ≤ or <.
Upper limit of a quantity or size range; unit in context.
Comparison sign for the lower value, e.g. ≥ or >.
Lower limit of a quantity or size range; unit in context.
Package size or filling quantity; unit e.g. L, mL, kg or g.
Packaging material, e.g. Kunststoff, Metall, Glas or Papier.
Further specifies the material and type of packaging.
This node and enclosed information are not required for the SDS, but helpful to identfy the packaged product and required for poison center notification according to CLP article 45.
Additional identification or product information.

At least one instance (with empty UserId) for the identification as delivered by the supplier. Use more instances for various package sizes, various products in a group SDS, or (with filled UserId) for reference to relabelled products of the SDS recipient. Also for group safety data sheets, each instance of TradeProductIdentity covers one substance or product. When importing, make sure that SDScom documents are not automatically replaced if the product identity is the same! GTINs are not necessarily unique (they should, but aren't in practice!), and product identities may refer to kits with multiple products and SDSs. Unique IDs that allow automatic overriding of data require a bilateral agreement between customer and supplier and should be placed in ProductNo.
Indicates whether industrial use is intended; yes/no or description.
Indicates whether professional use is intended; yes/no or description.
Indicates whether consumer use is intended; yes/no or description.
Describes any combination of industrial/professional/consumer in a way compatible e.g. to CLP article 45 poison center notification format.
General use or purpose of the product.
Uses advised against, including justification where applicable.

Name of the SDS. Shall be identical with the name on the hazard label and package unless the SDS is a group SDS, in which case the hazard label name must match one of the instances of TradeProductIdentity.

SDS not legally required: The formal requirements to SDSs do not apply to chemicals that legally do not require such documents. In this field, the reason for no legal requirement for an SDS can be stated.
Version No: The current version of the SDS document.
Date of issue: The date when this SDS was prepared for the first time.
Date of revision: The date of the last revision of the SDS document. See also EditingDate.

If the exporting system is the SDS authoring system, the value of EditingDate should be omitted or be equal to RevisionDate. If the export is prepared by another system, e.g. from a service provider, the EditingDate is the status of data entry of the SDS and is equal to or larger than RevisionDate.
Date when manufacturer stopped distribution. See also ProductDiscontinuedFromMarket.

Description of role: To describe an actor’s role. Accepted values: Responsible company, National responsible, Manufacturer, Importer, Only representative, Reimporter, Formulator, Distributor, Downstream user, Foreign manufacturer
Role description: Textual description of the role code. To allow language independent description in addition to English based role codes.
Description of role: To describe an actor’s role.
First line of the visiting address.
Second line of the visiting address.
Third line of the visiting address.
Postal code: Two-letter ISO3166 country code followed by a hyphen and the national postal code.
city of the visiting address.
Postal address: P.O.Box or street address
Second line of the postal address.
Third line of the postal address.
Postal code: Two-letter ISO3166 country code followed by a hyphen and the national postal code.
Postal city:
Address of the supplier, importer or contact person.
Telephone number:
Faximile number:
e-mail address to the company:
Company URL: Web address to the company’s home page
URL: Web addressof the company contact
National contact person or contact point for regional requirements.
Email address of the competent person responsible for the safety data sheet.
Company contact: This field covers all contact persons related to the company. Department or person within the company that can be contacted regarding information on the actual chemical.

The D-U-N-S Number references a legal entity and allows access to what could be considered a self-maintaining address book, created for the automotive and chemical industry. It should be added to any address in SDScom to help data integration. See also https://www.upik.de/
Supplier information: Contact information etc. on relevant actors in the supply chain.
Telephone number:
Information: This field is used to state what kind of assistance that can be obtained from the actual emergency telephone, if it is available only during office hours, etc.

Emergency phone: Contacts that can be used in case of an accident or trouble, e.g. the supplier’s own emergency phone or the phone number to an official advisory body. A Poison Information Center gives advice and instruction regarding treatment of acute poisoning caused by chemicals etc.
Region-specific information in the area of substance/mixture and supplier identification; jurisdiction follows from the field name.
Region-specific information in the area of substance/mixture and supplier identification; jurisdiction follows from the field name.
Exposure scenarios incorporated in the SDS: To state if the SDS is complete (eSDS) - meaning that the user has to adapt to the information in the SDS within 12 months.

Exposure scenarioes incorporated in the SDS: If the SDS is complete (an eSDS) - meaning that the user has to adapt to the information in the SDS within 12 months, the user must be informed about this. This element is to help the user distinguish between eSDSs and normal SDSs.
EuPCS code for product category under Annex VIII CLP; coded value.
full text product category for the EuPCS code.
main intended use of the product or substance; short description of the intended use.
Secondary or additional uses of the product.
REACH SU code for sector of use.
full text sector of use (SU).
Sector of use (SU):
REACH PC code for product category.
full text product category (PC).
Product category (PC):
REACH PROC code for process category.
full text process category (PROC).
Process category: PROC
REACH ERC code for environmental release category.
full text environmental release category (ERC).
Environment release category: ERC
SPERC code for specific environmental release category.
full text SPERC designation.
Specific environmental release category (SPERC) for the use.
REACH article category code (AC).
full text REACH article category (AC).
Article category without intended release; REACH use descriptor AC.
Article category with intended release; REACH use descriptor.
name of the exposure scenario.
File name if the exposure scenarios is available in EScom XML format.
Corresponding exposure scenario for the identified use.
Identifier of the identified use; technical or internal identifier.
Indicates whether the identified use is to be output as an annex; yes/no.

NB: Optional attribute IdentifiedUseId to identify the actual identified use (ExposureScenario). The optional attribute PrintAsAttachment can be used to toggle printing the exposue scenario inline in the Sds or as an attachment.
Product type: For trade product, e.g. detergent, paint, lubricant, glue
Function desription: This field can be used for product function description in free text.
Relevant identified use according to REACH/exposure scenario.
Region-specific information in the area of substance/mixture and supplier identification; jurisdiction follows from the field name.
Region-specific information in the area of substance/mixture and supplier identification; jurisdiction follows from the field name.
Identification data for the substance/mixture, uses and supplier.
Hazard class and category according to GHS/CLP-System; coded value.

Printable, phrase based representation of HazardClassCategory. While this may be identical to HazardClassCatgory in its string representation, it provides a translated version linked to a phrase library for applications where this is useful.
For Sepcific Target Organ Toxicity (STOT), one or more affected organs should be listed if known.

For Specific Target Organ Toxicity (STOT), the entry can be limited to a way of exposure (e.g. inhalation). Although there is currently no known case with more than one route of exposure, we cannot exclude this biologically and thus technically.

To state how the individual classification is prepared. (This information should be shown in section 16). Only relevant for instances of type Classification in section 2. For components in section 3, this info should not be part of the SDS.
Information on inhalation exposure or toxicity; typically expressed as % with explanatory text where applicable.
Information on dermal exposure or toxicity; typically expressed as % with explanatory text where applicable.
Information on oral exposure or toxicity; typically expressed as % with explanatory text where applicable.
Information on unknown aquatic toxicity; typically expressed as % with explanatory text.
Fraction or indication of unknown toxicity; typically expressed as % with explanatory text.

Acute Toxicity Estimate as provided by the supplier. Necessary according to UN GHS if the mixture is ingredient of another mixture, to derive this product's toxicity classification. In CLP, ATE values may also be specified in harmonized classifications (CLP Annex VI)
Additional information on classification: If the chemical do not meet the classification criteria etc.
according to GHS revision 5
Classification according to the rules specified for Argentina GHS/SDS rules.

Pictogram: A graphical presentation that includes a symbol plus other graphic elements, such as a border, background pattern or colour that is intended to convey specific information on the hazard concerned.
GHS signal word code, e.g. Danger or Warning.
Signal word: A word that indicates the relative level of severity of hazards to alert the reader to a potential hazard.
code of a hazard statement according to GHS-Revision 5, e.g. H-Satz.
Hazard statement: A phrase assigned to a hazard class and category that describes the nature of the hazards of a hazardous substance or mixture, including, where appropriate, the degree of hazard.
code of a precautionary statement according to GHS-Revision 5, e.g. P-Satz.
Precautionary statement: A phrase that describes recommended measure(s) to minimise or prevent adverse effects resulting from exposure to a hazardous substance or mixture due to its use or disposal.
Additional labelling information, e.g. special advice or supplemental information.
according to GHS revision 5
Hazard labelling: To collect all information on the trade product’s hazard labelling in one group.
Region-specific information for Argentina.
according to GHS revision 4
according to GHS revision 7. Adopted, but does not (yet) officially replace revision 4.
Classification according to the rules specified for Brazil GHS/SDS rules.
Region-specific information for Brazil.
Hazard classification according to WHMIS 2015; classes, categories and H-statements.
Classification in the Canadian WHMIS/GHS context.
Region-specific information for Canada.
Hazard classification according to the Chinese GB 30000 standards
Classification according to the rules specified for China GHS/SDS rules.
Region-specific information for China.
Hazard classification according to the applicable classification system; coded value or phrase.
Acute M-factor or acute assessment value; dimensionless, if M-factor.
Chronic M-factor or chronic assessment value; dimensionless, if M-factor.

Multiplying factor for substances highly toxic to the environment. Part of the classification of pure substances. The M factors are used in application of summation method for classification of mixtures containing substances that are classified as very toxic. The concept of M factors has been established to give an increased weight to very toxic substances when classifying mixtures.
Supplemental hazard information or EUH/additional statement.
always interpreted as greater than or equal to the value
always interpreted as less than (not equal) to the value. If omitted, max percentage is 100.
As provided by a harmonized classification or the supplier for dilutions of the substance/product. There is not just one SCL per hazard class, so this cannot be bound to such classes.
code of supplemental hazard information in the ATP/CLP context.

Supplemental Hazards are treated in CLP as labelling elements, but in fact are assessed like other classifications. For mixtures, supplemental hazards of ingredients need to be known to determine supplemental hazards of the mixture. Thus, systems can duplicate the information available as labelling here. See also https://github.com/esdscom/sdscom-xml/issues/229

Classification notes: To identify classification notes (letters and/or figures) in the case that the trade product is a substance. This information shall be stated in the SDS together with the classifications of the substance.
The chemical’s individual hazard classifications according to GB-CLP (2020), which adopted EU regulation 1272/2008 as modified by ATP 12.
Classification according to UK CLP or the British CLP regulation.
Region-specific information for Great Britain.
according to GHS revision 5
Classification according to the rules specified for Mexico GHS/SDS rules.
Region-specific information for Mexico.
The chemical’s individual hazard classifications according to SEA (2021), which adopted EU regulation 1272/2008 as modified by ATP 12.
Classification according to the GHS/SDS rules specified for Turkey.
Region-specific information for Turkey.
Classification according to 29 CFR 1910.1200
Classification according to US-HazCom/GHS-Kontext.

Hazard identification: Description of the most important hazardous effects connected to the chemical in normal use and foreseeable misuse. This element should not be used in the compilation of SDSs - only to receive information from existing SDSs in import!
Physicochemical effects: The most important adverse physicochemical effects and symptoms.
Health effects: The most important adverse health effects and symptoms.
Environmental effects: The most important adverse environmental effects and symptoms.
Effects of misuse: Description of the most important adverse effects and symptoms of possible misuses that can be reasonably foreseen.
Ohter hazards: Other hazards necessary to mention which do not result in classification, but which contribute to overall hazards.

Other hazards: Hazards which do not result in classification but which may contribute to the overall hazards of the substance or mixture, such as formation of air contaminants during hardening or processing, dustiness, dust explosion hazards, cross-sensitisation, suffocation, freezing, high potency for odour or taste, or environmental effects like hazards to soil-dwelling organisms, or photochemical ozone creation potential.
Region-specific information for USA.
Hazards identification including classification, labelling and other hazards.
was "DescriptionOfTheMixture" up to v4.2.3; see issue #95
Composition or information on ingredients of a substance or mixture, including relevant hazardous constituents.

General first aid measures: Brief and easy to understand informationfor the victim, bystanders and first-aiders. Information if immediate medical attention is required, on what can be done on the spot in the case of an accident, and whether delayed effects can be expected after exposure.
First aid inhalation: First aid measures to be taken after inhalation of the chemical.
First aid skin: First aid measures to be taken after skin contact with the chemical.
First aid eyes: First aid measures to be taken if the chemical gets in contact with the eyes.
First aid ingestion: First aid measures to be taken after ingestion of the chemical.
Personal protection for first aider: Information on personal protective equipment to be used by rescuers.
Description of first aid measures, understandable also for untrained first responders.
most important acute and delayed symptoms and effects after exposure.
Acute symptoms and effects: Information on
Delayed symptoms and effects: Information on delayed symptoms
Information to physician:
Medical treatment: Information on
Required clinical testing: Information on the need of clinical testing.
Required medical monitoring: Information on
Specific antidotes: Information on
Contraindications: Information on

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Medical Attention And Special Treatment Needed

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Medical Attention And Special Treatment Needed

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Medical attention and special treatment needed: Information if immediate medical attention or special medical treatment is needed after exposure to the chemical.
Specific first aid equipment: Information about specific equipment that must be available at the work place for instantaneous specific treatment in case of an accident.
First aid measures according to Exposition; structured by route of exposure and urgency.
Suitable extinguishing media: Extinguishing media that can be used.
Unsuitable media: Media that must not be applied in case of a fire.
Suitable and unsuitable extinguishing media for fires involving or near the product.
Fire and explosion hazards: Elements of risk in case of a fire or explosion, for instance a particular risk of exposure to the chemical or its decomposition products.
Hazardous combustion products: Information on hazardous components that may be formed during combustion of the chemical.
Precautionary measures in case of fire fighting: Measures and special protective equipment for fire-fighters.
Fire fighting procedures: Information on how to handle a fire in the chemical.
Special protective equipment for emergency responders, e.g. respiratory protection, protective clothing or cooling.
Requirements and advice for firefighting for the substance or mixture.
Personal precautions for non-emergency personnel: Advice on protective equipment etc.
Required personal protective equipment to prevent skin, eye or clothing contact.
Emergency procedures for release, e.g. evacuate the hazard area, remove ignition sources, consult experts.
Advice for non-emergency personnel during accidental release, e.g. distance, ventilation, personal protection equipment (PPE) and evacuation.
For emergency responders: Information on personal protection, suitable fabric for personal protective clothing, etc.
Environmental precautions: Information on preventive measures to be taken to protect environment.
Containment: Advice on how to contain a spill.

Cleaning up: Ways of cleaning-up spills, for instance by application of absorbing material, and the application of water to dilute effluent or restrict emission of gas or fume. Description of cleaning-up methods may be divided into small and large spills (specifications must be made by the individual SDS preparer).
Methods and materials for containment and cleaning up for leaks or releases; where applicable different measures depending on release quantity.
If appropriate, reference should be made to information in for instance section 8 and 13.

Accidental release measures: Information on response to spills - in cases where the spill volume has an impact on the hazard, distinguish between responses to large and small spills. If different practices for containment and recovery are required, this should be indicated.
Handling precautions: Recommendations to allow safe handling of the chemical, such as containment etc.
Safe handling of gas containers: Recommendations and instructions on handling of gas botles and containers to prevent acidents and damages.
Protective measures for safe handling and exposure prevention.
Measures to prevent fire and ignition hazards.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Measures To Prevent Aerosol And Dust

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Measures To Prevent Aerosol And Dust

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Measures to prevent aerosol or dust formation.
Measures to prevent release to the environment, drains or surface water.
Precautions for safe use, e.g. fire, dust or environmental protection.

Advice on general occupational hygiene, such as not to eat, drink and smoke in work areas, to wash hands after use, and to remove contaminated clothing and protective equipment before entering eating areas.
Advice on safe handling including protective, hygiene and environmental measures.

Storage precautions: Advice on specific storage requirements. How to manage possible risks associated with explosive atmospheres, corrosive conditions, flammability hazards, incompatible chemicals, evaporative conditions, and potential ignition sources. Advices may, if relevant, include ventilation requirements, specific designs for storage rooms or vessels, and quantity limits under storage conditions.
Conditions to avoid: Materials that must not get in contact with each other during storage etc.
Technical measures and storage conditions: Conditions required for safe storage of the chemical.
Packaging materials: Material and type of container to be used and packaging compabilities.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Requirements For Storage Rooms And Vessels

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Requirements For Storage Rooms And Vessels

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Requirements for storage rooms and vessels: Specific design for storage rooms or vessels (including retention walls and ventilation), incompatible materials, conditions of storage (temperature and humidity limit/range, light, inert gas, etc.) special electrical equipment and prevention of static electricity.
Advice on storage compatibility with other substances or mixtures.
Value with unit, e.g. numeric measured value and unit of measure.
Method or procedure used to determine the stated property.
Reference to test report, method, standard or literature source.
Reason why testing or information is not required or not available.
Permitted or recommended storage temperature; unit typically °C.
Permitted or recommended storage pressure; unit typically Pa, kPa, hPa or bar.
Permitted or recommended storage humidity; typically expressed in % relative humidity.
Pressure value; typically expressed in Pa, kPa, hPa or bar.
Maximum storage period under specified conditions; unit e.g. Tage, Monate or Jahre.
Information on the use of stabilisers or antioxidants that are required to maintain the integrity of the chemical
Conditions for safe storage: Information on how to control the effects of weather conditions, ambient pressure, temperature, sunlight, humidity, vibration etc.
Recommendations for specific end uses or safe application.
Industrial sector specific solutions: Information on industrial sector specific solutions.

For substances and mixtures designed for specific end use(s), recommendations shall relate to the identified use(s) and be detailed and operational. If industry or sector specific guidance is available, detailed reference to it (including source and issuing date) may be made.

Handling and storage: Advice on safe handling practices with emphasise on precautions that are appropriate to the identified uses referred to under subsection 1.2 and to the unique properties of the chemical. Information shall relate to the protection of human health, safety and the environment. It shall assist the employer in devising suitable working procedures and organisational measures according to Article 5 of Directive 98/24/EC and Article 5 of Directive 2004/37/EC. Where a chemical safety report is required, the information shall be consistent with the information given for the identified uses in the chemical safety report and the exposure scenarios showing control of risk.
Indicates whether occupational medical surveillance is required; yes/no or justification.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Limit Value Type With Country Or Organisation

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Limit Value Type With Country Or Organisation

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: type of limit value with country or organisation, e.g. AGW (DE), IOELV (EU) or MAK.
If two occurences, one must be ppm and the other a matching mg/m3 value.
Numeric value or range with unit and qualifier, e.g. >, <, approx. or interval.
Assessment period for short-term exposure limits; unit typically min or h.
If two occurences, one must be ppm and the other a matching mg/m3 value.
Peak limitation overflow factor for short-term exposure limits; dimensionless factor.

Also known as ceiling value. If two occurences, one must be ppm and the other a matching mg/m3 value. One of Value and PeakLimitationOverflowFactor is sufficient. If both are given, Value must be the short-term Value multiplied with the overflow factor.
Recommended measurement or monitoring procedure for relevant exposures.
Particle fraction for occupational exposure limits, e.g. inhalable or respirable.
Source or reference for limit values, tests or data; bibliographic or URL.
aims at the product in delivery state
aims at degradation product limit values during use

Occupational exposure limit: Values shall be given for the country where the substance or preparation is placed on the market. Give information on currently recommended monitoring procedures. For mixtures, it is useful to provide values for those constituent substances which are required to be listed in the Safety Data Sheet.
Investigation parameter in biological monitoring, e.g. metabolite or marker parameter.
Tested matrix or sample, e.g. blood, urine, air, water, soil or test material.
date of test or analysis.
aims at the product in delivery state
aims at degradation product limit values during use

Biological limit value: aims at the product in delivery state. Information regarding biological limit values - e.g. concentration of lead in blood. Biological limits will refer to individual components, not preparations.
Short code of the exposure group; coded value.
Full designation der exposure group, e.g. industrial user or consumer.
Exposure group for DNEL/DMEL, e.g. workers, consumers or general population.
type of effect level, e.g. acute/long-term, local/systemic; coded value.
full text description of the effect level type.
Exposure route, frequency and type of effect:
Derived No-Effect Level (DNEL); unit depends on exposure route and population.
May be important in those cases where the DNEL is very low and where more than 1 DNEL existing to show how high the influence on the deviation was.

Derived no effect level (DNEL): Where a Chemical Safety Report is required, the relevant DNELs for the substance shall be given. For preparations, it is useful to provide values for those constituent substances which are required to be listed in the safety data sheet.
Derived Minimal Effect Level (DMEL); unit depends on exposure route and population.
DMEL data for exposure routes, where no safe threshold can be derived.
PNEC compartment or type, e.g. freshwater, marine water, soil, sediment or sewage treatment plant.
Predicted No-Effect Concentration (PNEC); unit depends on environmental compartment, often mg/L.

Predicted no effect concentration (PNEC): Where a Chemical Safety Report is required, the relevant PNECs for the substance shall be given. For preparations, it is useful to provide values for those constituent substances which are required to be listed.
Region-specific information in the area of exposure controls and personal protection; jurisdiction follows from the field name.
Exposure limits and control parameters, e.g. occupational exposure limits, DNEL, DMEL or PNEC.
Summary of worker-related risk management measures.
Summary of environmental risk management measures.
Description of the task or use activity in the risk management context.
Hazard band in the control-banding system; coded or categorised information.
Scale of use or amount used; qualitative information or Menge with unit.
Potential for release into air, e.g. dustiness or volatility; qualitative information.
Intended control approach, e.g. general ventilation, local exhaust or closed installation.
Control-banding approach to derive risk management measures; model or category.
Summary of risk management measures for safe use.
Engineering controls, e.g. closed systems, local exhaust ventilation or process ventilation.
Product-related risk reduction measures, e.g. formulation, packaging or dosing.
Instructional or behavioural measures for safe use and exposure control.
Organisational protection measures, e.g. work procedures, access restrictions or training.
Organisational signs or notices, e.g. warning, prohibition or mandatory signs.
Technical risk reduction measures, e.g. enclosure, ventilation or containment.
Technical labels or signs on installations or work equipment.
Suitable engineering, organisational and personal measures to reduce exposure.
General information on respiratory protection and its conditions of use.
Conditions, tasks or exposures, where respiratory protection is required.
Tasks where respiratory protection is required or recommended.
Suitable respiratory protective equipment including filter class or device type.
self-rescue equipment for emergencies, e.g. escape filter or respiratory hood.
Respiratory mask type, e.g. half mask, full face mask or particulate filtering mask.
Filter device type for respiratory protection, e.g. half mask, full face mask or powered air-purifying respirator.
type or category of the named element; coded or described by phrase.
Manufacturer of the product, equipment or protective article.
Source of supply or supplier for equipment, product or protective article.
Reference relevant standard: Only to be used for referencing old standards for compatibility
Recommended respiratory protective devices or filter types according to the exposure situation.
Additional respiratory protection measures, e.g. ventilation, wear-time limitation or emergency equipment.
Respiratory protection measures for exposure to gases, vapours, mists or dusts.
Required protective properties of the equipment, e.g. chemical resistance or standard compliance.
Suitable eye protection equipment according to hazard and exposure potential.
Unsuitable eye protection equipment or materials for the specified application.
Specific eye protection equipment, e.g. safety glasses, goggles or face shield.
Additional eye protection measures, e.g. eye shower, face shield or splash protection.
eye/face protection measures to prevent contact with eyes or face.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Skin Hand Protection Short Term Contact

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Skin Hand Protection Short Term Contact

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: hand protection requirements for short-term or occasional contact.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Skin Hand Protection Long Term Contact

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Skin Hand Protection Long Term Contact

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: hand protection requirements for long-term or permanent contact.
Unsuitable materials, that do not provide sufficient protection or resistance.
Required properties of hand protection, e.g. chemical resistance and breakthrough time.
Suitable glove type according to contact type and exposure duration.
Suitable material, e.g. nitrile, butyl rubber or Viton, depending on resistance.
Glove material breakthrough time; typically expressed in min.
Glove material thickness; typically expressed in mm.
Maximum wear duration for occasional contact; typically expressed in min or h.
Maximum wear duration for permanent contact; typically expressed in min or h.
Specific protective article or equipment item; text or product designation.
Equipment or protective article for the described protection or application purpose.
Additional hand protection measures, e.g. skin protection plan, change intervals or cleaning.
hand protection measures including glove type, material, thickness and breakthrough time.
Suitable protective clothing according to substance properties and exposure.
Unsuitable protective clothing or materials for the described exposure.
Required properties of protective clothing, e.g. chemical resistance or flame protection.
Recommended protective clothing material according to hazard and contact type.
Recommended protective clothing articles, e.g. coverall, apron, boots or arm protection.
Additional skin protection measures, e.g. protective clothing, cleaning or skin protection products.
Other skin or body protection other than hand protection.
body protection measures to prevent skin contact or contamination.
Protective measures against thermal hazards, e.g. heat, cold or burns.
Specific hygiene measures, e.g. wash hands, remove contaminated clothing.
Normally to be displayed or printed at the top of section 8. In case of using information from components, duplicates should be removed.
Personal protective equipment, required or recommended for safe use.
Environmental exposure controls and risk management measures for emissions to air, water or soil.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Measures On Consumer Use Of The Chemical

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Measures On Consumer Use Of The Chemical

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: risk management measures for consumers during use of the substance or mixture.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Measures On Service Life In Articles

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Measures On Service Life In Articles

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Measures to limit exposure during the service life of articles.
Measures to limit consumer exposure during use or service life of articles.

aas:langStringNameType.aas:text: Exposure Controls Personal Protection Additional Info

aas:langStringPreferredNameTypeIec61360.aas:text: Exposure Controls Personal Protection Additional Info

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Additional information on exposure controls and personal protective equipment.

Exposure control and personal protection: This section shall describe the applicable occupational exposure limits and necessary risk management measures. Where a chemical safety report is required, the information in this section shall be consistent with the chemical safety report and the exposure scenarios showing control of risk from the chemical safety report set out in the annex to the safety data sheet.
form or appearance of the product, e.g. powder, granulate, liquid or paste.

aas:valueReferencePair.aas:value: gas under pressure: refrigerated liquefied gas

aas:langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.aas:text: Indicate the form (solid, liquid, gas or other descriptive terms) of the substance or mixture as supplied. May be omitted if specified in field Form. If Form is "other", put more details in this field.
Physical state (only solid/liquid/gaseous) under standard conditions (20°C, 1013 hpa)
Physical state under standard conditions.
Physical state under standard conditions; gas, liquid or solid.
Multiple entries (only) in case of "multicolour" and "colouring agent"
Product colour: Indicate the colour of the substance or preparation as supplied. May be omitted if Colour is used. This field is also used if none of ColourEnum matches.
Colour intensity of the product; qualitative information.

Physical and chemical properties: This section of the safety data sheet shall describe the empirical data relating to the substance or mixture, if relevant. In the case of a mixture, the entries shall clearly indicate to which substance in the mixture the data apply, unless it is valid for the whole mixture. The following properties shall be clearly identified including, where appropriate, a reference to the test methods used and specification of appropriate units of measurement and/or reference conditions. If relevant for the interpretation of the numerical value, the method of determination shall also be provided.

Reactivity description: The reactivity hazards of the chemical shall be described. Specific test data shall be provided where available. Information may also be based on general data for the class or family of substance or mixture if such data adequately represent the anticipated hazard.If data for mixtures are not available, data on substances in the mixture shall be provided.

Stability description: The stability of the substance or preparation and the possibility of hazardous reactions occurring. Specify the need of stabilizer, the possibility of hazardous reaction (e.g. exothermic reaction), safety significance of a possible change in physical characteristics of the chemical, etc.

Hazardous reactions: If relevant, state if the chemical will react or polymerise, releasing excess pressure or heat, or creating other hazardous conditions. The conditions under which the hazardous reactions may occur shall be described.

Materials to avoid – incompatible materials: Families of substances or mixtures or specific substances, such as water, air, acids, bases, oxidising agents, with which the substance or mixture could react to produce a hazardous situation shall be listed. If appropriate, give a brief description of measures to be taken.

Hazardous decomposition products: Hazardous chemicals which may be formed in dangerous quantity during decomposition. Address specifically hazardous decomposition products, if any, formed upon contact with water, and possibility of degradation to unstable products. Hazardous combustion products shall be included in Section 5.

Stability and reactivity: The section shall describe the stability of the chemical and the possibility of hazardous reactions occurring under certain conditions of use, also if released into the environment. Where appropriate, include a reference to the test methods used. If a particular property does not apply or if information is not available, the reasons shall be given.

Waste treatment containers and methods shall be specified including the appropriate methods of waste treatment of both the chemical and any contaminated packaging (e.g. incineration, recycling, landfilling).
